report.source_text: The postoperative pathology of the left axillary mass combined with morphological and immunohistochemical results was consistent with Paget disease. The pathological examination of the skin lesions showed an abundance of keratinization in the epidermis, a large number of atypical cells in the epithelial layer, infiltration of interstitial lymphocytes, and infiltration of Paget cells in the superficial dermis (Fig. 2). Postoperative immunohistochemistry showed estrogen receptor (+, 20%), progesterone receptor (−), human epidermal growth factor receptor-2 (3+), Ki-67 (30%), cytokine (CK)7 (+), and p63 (−) (Fig. 3).

report.source_text: Treatment process: The patient was placed in a supine position and under general anesthesia, left subaxillary mass resection, freezing and left breast cancer breast conserving surgery was performed. We covered the affected area with gauze before cutting the skin and fix the skin. We made a shuttle shaped incision 1.5 cm outside the lesion area, approximately 7 cm in length, and separated toward the deep. During the surgery, the size of the tissue, including the lesion, was approximately 7 cm × 5 cm and frozen during the surgery (Fig. 1B). The results showed that fibrous adipose tissue can be seen in the left armpit, and a large number of inflammatory cells infiltrate.

clinician.final_diagnosis: The postoperative pathology of the left axillary mass combined with morphological and immunohistochemical results was consistent with Paget disease.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 57-year-old female presented with a 2-year history of a left axillary mass, which recently increased in size and ulcerated. An initial resection at Jiangxi Provincial Dermatology Hospital yielded pathology consistent with Paget disease outside the armpit breast. The patient was subsequently admitted to the reporting hospital where a left subaxillary mass resection and left breast cancer breast conserving surgery were performed. Postoperative pathology, including morphological findings (abundance of keratinization, atypical cells in epithelial layer, interstitial lymphocyte infiltration, Paget cells in superficial dermis) and immunohistochemistry (ER 20%, PR -, HER2 3+, Ki-67 30%, CK7 +, p63 -), confirmed Paget disease. A 16-month follow-up showed no local recurrence, lymph node swelling, distant metastasis, or complications.
